scope: Primary-source findings and original project notes; no full paper copies or model training

sources.title: Droplet slipperiness despite surface heterogeneity at molecular scale
sources.readScope: Publisher full text, abstract and contact-line friction equation
sources.finding: Contact angle and contact-line friction must be distinguished; both hydrophilic and hydrophobic tested SAM surfaces can have low friction.
sources.modelUse: Separate equilibrium shape, advancing/receding angles and dynamic resistance.
sources.notEstablished: Does not measure our visor or give universal polycarbonate material constants.

sources.title: Solution Crystallization of Polycarbonate Surfaces for Hydrophobic State: Water Droplet Dynamics and Life Cycle Assessment towards Self-Cleaning Applications
sources.readScope: Publisher indexed abstract, discussion and Table1; direct page429 and PMC browser challenge
sources.finding: The tested untreated PC and two crystallized PC surfaces differed in contact angle and hysteresis; high apparent contact angle did not eliminate pinning.
sources.modelUse: A substrate name alone cannot prescribe coating behaviour; retain high-pinning controls.
sources.notEstablished: These solvent-textured PV samples are not racing helmet visor measurements or a coating recommendation.

sources.title: Maximal deformation of an impacting drop
sources.finding: Reports low-viscosity impact spreading scaling with Weber number to the one-quarter power in the investigated regimes.
sources.modelUse: Use normal impact speed, size and liquid properties for bounded spread estimates, separately from subsequent wetting/retention.
sources.notEstablished: Not a universal splash, rebound or deposited-film fraction law at arbitrary high-speed grazing visor impact.

sources.title: Hydrodynamic Theory of Forced Dewetting
sources.readScope: Publisher abstract, full text subscription gated
sources.finding: A bath-withdrawal contact line has a critical-speed transition to film deposition.
sources.modelUse: Treat film deposition as regime dependent; capillary-number scaling is an approximation.
sources.notEstablished: Does not establish that every moving finite droplet on a visor leaves a Landau-Levich film or determine our coefficient.

sources.title: Pinlock anti-fog technology
sources.finding: The insert uses moisture absorption and a sealed thermal barrier.
sources.modelUse: Keep interior condensation/insert behaviour separate from exterior rain wetting.
sources.notEstablished: Does not identify the coating or temperature of our target visor, or imply exterior water repellency.

sources.title: IAPWS R9-97: Release on the Refractive Index of Ordinary Water Substance
sources.readScope: Release formulation, wavelength/temperature/density scope and verification table
sources.finding: Water refractive index depends on wavelength, temperature and density.
sources.modelUse: Keep water optics distinct from substrate and camera geometry; fixed visible-water approximation is an explicit gameplay simplification.
sources.notEstablished: Not justification for changing water index simply because the substrate changes from a windscreen to a visor.

sources.title: Local CSP728 RainFX DXBC inspection
sources.finding: Named velocity/map movement/fade/trace filtering/finalization passes exist.
sources.modelUse: Study the separation of physical state and efficient presentation maps.
sources.notEstablished: Recovered shader constants are not SI material parameters, and CPU timing/bindings remain unknown.
